questions.q: Which of the following is unstructured data?
options: A CSV file with a fixed schema
A corpus of emails and attachments
questions.explain: Emails and attachments have no predefined schema: unstructured. Tables, CSVs, and ERP records are structured.

questions.q: A disk is encrypted at rest. An attacker steals the powered-off laptop. Is the data protected?
options: No, encryption at rest never protects data
Yes, as long as the key is unavailable and the system is powered off
No, because the disk can be copied
Yes, but only if the disk is an SSD
questions.explain: Encryption at rest protects a stolen or powered-off medium. It does not protect a booted and unlocked system.

questions.q: An attacker uses a compromised service account to exfiltrate data via a legitimate query. Why did encryption at rest not protect the data?
options: Because encryption at rest is obsolete
Because the data was in use and accessible to the authorized account
Because the key was stored in an HSM
Because the database was not backed up
questions.explain: The database decrypts data to answer the query: the attacker acts as an authorized user. Least privilege, DLP, and exfiltration detection are needed.

questions.q: To which data state does TLS encryption primarily apply?
questions.explain: TLS protects data moving across the network. At rest, disk encryption or TDE is used.

questions.q: A customer service operator must see the last four digits of a card, never the full number. Which method is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Masking displays only part of the value (****1234) without exposing the full data. Tokenization would replace the entire value with a token.

questions.q: A merchant needs to reference cards for customer service without storing the real number. Which method should be chosen?
questions.explain: Tokenization replaces the number with a token and stores the mapping in a protected vault. Hashing would prevent reuse; masking would not allow looking up the card.

questions.q: Which statement about de-identification is accurate?
options: It can often be re-identified by cross-referencing datasets
questions.explain: De-identification removes or generalizes identifiers, but cross-referencing can re-identify individuals. True anonymization is irreversible and hard to prove.

questions.q: Who decides the classification of data and its associated permissions?
questions.explain: The data owner is a business leader who decides classification and access. The custodian implements the controls.

questions.q: A system administrator applies backups and encryption to an HR database. What role do they play?
questions.explain: They implement and maintain controls: they are a custodian. They do not decide who is allowed to read HR data.

questions.q: Which stage of the data lifecycle is the right time to classify data?
questions.explain: Classification must be decided at creation, as it triggers storage, access, and destruction controls.

questions.q: At which stage does an egress DLP primarily operate?
questions.explain: Egress DLP inspects data leaving the perimeter: this is the sharing stage. It can also act at storage, but egress is its primary enforcement point.

questions.q: A legal hold is issued. What happens to the 30-day destruction policy?
options: It is suspended for the affected data
questions.explain: A legal hold suspends destruction, even if the policy specifies 30 days. Destroying evidence after notification can result in sanctions.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes internal classification from regulatory category?
options: 'Confidential' is a legal obligation; 'health data' is an internal classification
'Confidential' is an internal classification; 'health data' is a regulatory category
questions.explain: Internal classification organizes the organization's rules; regulatory category triggers legal obligations (GDPR, HIPAA). Both complement each other.

questions.q: Match each method to its primary characteristic.
questions.explain: Four different levels of reversibility. The choice depends on the use case: display, referencing, integrity, or confidentiality.

questions.q: Which controls relate to protecting data in use? (Select all that apply)
options: DLP monitoring access to sensitive data
questions.explain: Data in use: isolation, least privilege, DLP. TLS protects data in transit, not processing in memory.
